title: Buglands
summary: A concept to retheme the Costa Rica Climber as Buglands, a playground of bug habitats.
overview: I rethemed the Costa Rica Climber in Thanksgiving Point’s Butterfly Biosphere. The play structure was not really working, and there was not much theming. I walked the climber and photographed it, then developed Buglands: regions themed to different kinds of bugs. I built a concept deck for the whole idea and modeled a few touchpoints.
role: I led the concept: site research, the theme and story, the concept deck, and the first 3D touchpoint models.
challenge: I had to retheme the existing Costa Rica Climber. It was not really working as a play structure, and the space had little theming.
heroCaption: Opening slide of the concept deck, “The Buglands.”
heroAlt: Concept illustration from the Buglands deck, titled The Buglands.

regions.name: Colony Cliffs
regions.text: Bug communities: ants, termites, and social wasps. In the deck this is the entrance, where colony builders make tunnels, chambers, and towers.

regions.name: Hopper Plains
regions.text: The toddler area. Grassland and grasshoppers: soft fields for bouncing, leaping, and playing from a grasshopper’s view.

regions.name: Wetland Wonders
regions.text: Water habitat: diving beetles, water striders, whirligigs, and scorpions in arid riverbeds. The deck also calls this Bug Basin.

regions.name: Bug Borough
regions.text: Underground or forest-floor bugs. Tunnels, bioluminescence, glowworms, isopods, beetles, roaches, and decomposers.

regions.name: Canopy Crossing
regions.text: Above, in the rainforest canopy: tropical insects, stick bugs, and assassin bugs. The deck splits the canopy into Build a Bug, Find a Bug, Fly a Bug, and the Butterfly Passage.

title: Jurassic Jungle: Shoe Room Story Video
summary: A video for the shoe-room monitor, so guests understand the story before they enter the playground.
overview: Jurassic Jungle is a kids’ playground with a story throughout. Kids wear interactive wristbands to log their progress as they find missing hatchlings and return them to their nest. I owned the touchpoint in the shoe room, before guests enter.
role: I designed the touchpoint and made the motion and video in After Effects.
challenge: I needed guests to understand the story and the instructions before they entered the chaotic playground. Signage was already there. Early on, very few people stopped to read it, and guests said they didn’t know what was going on at first. I made a video for the monitor to increase dwell time and understanding.
steps: I observed guests and logged what I saw.
I planned the key messages to deliver.
I built it in After Effects over several iterations, tightening the visuals and using animation to direct attention.
I installed the video on the TV.
I fixed the volume and the gap between loops, and I shipped those edits for day 2.
outcome: After I installed the video, I saw more dwell time and more attention from both kids and parents. That read is qualitative. I did not record counts.

title: Jurassic Jungle: Locker Area Prop Concept
summary: A prop concept for the locker area, starting from an off-the-shelf clear hinged enclosure.
overview: I designed a prop concept for the Jurassic Jungle locker area. The rendering styles a clear hinged enclosure as a sci-fi specimen case holding an “Apatosaurus Skull,” with a holographic teal overlay, HUD graphics, a touch-point icon, and a stand. It shows a side view and a front view.
role: I designed a prop concept for the locker area.

title: Jurassic Hall Kids Area: Measured Model
summary: Detailed measurements and a SketchUp model of the kids’ area under the ascending ramp.
overview: I took detailed measurements and built a SketchUp model of the kids’ area in Jurassic Hall at Thanksgiving Point.
role: I measured the kids’ area and built the SketchUp model.
challenge: The room was especially hard for me to model because of its odd shape: structural poles and a sloping ceiling. The space sits underneath the ascending ramp.

title: Jurassic Hall Exhibit Upgrade: Install Team
summary: I helped measure the room and the ramp behind the exhibit, and I was on the team for the install of its first upgrade.
overview: The first upgrade of the juvenile Stegosaurus display in Jurassic Hall. I helped measure the room and the ramp behind the exhibit, and I was on the team during the install.
role: I helped measure the room and the ramp behind the exhibit. I was on the install team for this upgrade. I did not design the exhibit or run the fabrication.
gained: I saw, firsthand, how the team coordinates with the fabrication shop and with vendors during an install.

title: Design Study: Kidstopia Concept Documents
summary: A study of other designers’ concept drawings for Kidstopia, so I could learn play touchpoints and what each one is for.
overview: I studied the concept drawings for the Kidstopia venue at the Museum of Natural Curiosity, Thanksgiving Point. I was learning the different types of play touchpoints and the purposes they serve. I did not create these drawings.
